questions.question: A news site has 40,000 product photos that need a one-sentence description for thumbnails. Which approach meets the requirement with the least effort?

options.text: Send each image to a multimodal chat deployment with a prompt that requests a single concise sentence
options.why: Correct. A multimodal model returns text, and the prompt controls the length and style.

options.text: Train a custom image classification model
options.why: Classification returns labels, not descriptive sentences.

options.text: Use text-embedding models on the image file names
options.why: Embeddings of file names do not describe the content of the pictures.

options.text: Use gpt-image to redraw each photo
options.why: Image generation creates new pictures. It does not describe existing ones.

questions.explanation: A vision-enabled chat model accepts images and a prompt. A concise caption prompt gives short descriptions for thumbnails.

questions.question: An insurance application asks a multimodal model about a photo: 'How old is the car?' The model must not guess when the photo does not show the answer. What should the developer configure?

options.text: A system message that tells the model to answer only from visible evidence and to say when it cannot tell
options.why: Correct. Grounding instructions reduce speculation.

options.text: A higher temperature
options.why: A higher temperature increases variation and the risk of guesses.

options.text: A larger value for n
options.why: The n parameter controls the number of completions, not grounding.

options.text: Detail set to low
options.why: Detail affects image resolution, not whether the model guesses.

questions.explanation: Visual question answering is grounded by instructing the model to use visible evidence and to state that it cannot tell when the image does not show the answer.

questions.question: A web team must generate alt text for informative images. Which instruction best follows accessibility guidance?

options.text: Describe every pixel region in as much detail as possible
options.why: Alt text must be short. Long descriptions belong in an extended description.

options.text: Start every description with 'Image of'
options.why: Screen readers already announce an image, so this wording adds noise.

options.text: Return only the file name
options.why: A file name does not describe the content.

options.text: Describe the purpose of the image briefly, include meaningful text shown in the image, and return an empty value for decorative images
options.why: Correct. This follows common alt text guidance.

questions.explanation: Alt text states the purpose briefly and includes meaningful text. Decorative images get empty alt text, and complex images can have a separate extended description.

questions.question: An application sends 12 images in one request to a multimodal chat deployment to compare them. The request fails. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Images must be sent one at a time
options.why: Several images can be sent in the same request, up to the limit.

options.text: The detail parameter must be set to high
options.why: The detail parameter does not remove the image limit.

options.text: A single request is limited to 10 images
options.why: Correct. Split the images into several requests.

options.text: The deployment type must be Provisioned
options.why: The deployment type does not set the number of images in a request.

questions.explanation: A request can include up to 10 images. Send larger sets in batches and combine the results in the application.

questions.question: An application reads small printed text in photographs of delivery labels, but the model often misses characters. The application sets detail to low to save cost. What should the developer change?

options.text: Switch to a gpt-image deployment
options.why: Image generation models do not read text from photographs for analysis.

options.text: Set the temperature to 2
options.why: Temperature does not improve what the model can see.

options.text: Send the image as a URL instead of base64
options.why: The transport method does not change the resolution used for analysis.

options.text: Set detail to high so the model sees the image at higher resolution
options.why: Correct. High detail processes more of the image and helps with small text.

questions.explanation: The detail setting trades cost and speed against fidelity. Low reads a reduced version of the image, so small text can be missed.
